newsitem.title: INDIA: British Gas mulls $1.5bn India investments.
newsitem.headline: British Gas mulls $1.5bn India investments.

text.p: British Gas is currently assessing the potential for investing $1.5 billion in India, Gerard Rees, the company's country general manager in India told Reuters on Wednesday.
The company is engaged in a feasibility study to bring in, distribute and sell liquified natural gas (LNG) in India. The study will be completed in August.
It has also pre-qualified for the competitive bid stage to set up a 615 MW dual-fuel fired power plant at Pipavav in the west Indian state of Gujarat. Bids had to be lodged by May 6.
British Gas is also in a joint venture, named Mahanagar Gas, with Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) to pipe 1.5 million cubic metres of natural gas to customers in Bombay.

The venture already has 2,500 domestic customers, and expects to have 8,000 by the end of the year. The 10-year project, which is estimated to cost $150 million, aims to finally connect 600,000-650,000 customers in the city.
British Gas has also set up a joint venture with an Indian unit of the British security company Group 4 to provide services like meter reading for the emerging gas consumer market.
